rows.label: Concept
rows.text: One molecule, three serviceable notations above the molecular formula. The **structural formula** draws every bond — complete but slow. The **condensed (contracted) formula** writes groups in sequence — CH₃CH₂OH, CH₃COOH — preserving connectivity while staying fast, and unlike the molecular formula it distinguishes isomers (ethanol CH₃CH₂OH vs dimethyl ether CH₃OCH₃, both C₂H₆O).…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***One formula, two compounds*** — C2H6O is ethanol and dimethyl ether alike; write CH3CH2OH or CH3OCH3 and the ambiguity disappears — the condensed formula is the cheapest cure for isomer blindness.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The molecular formula is the only notation that loses information: C2H6O hides two different compounds, and only the condensed formula CH3CH2OH vs CH3OCH3 restores the identity.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Molecular formula: atom counts only (C2H6O) — cannot distinguish isomers. Structural formula: every bond drawn explicitly (H-C-C-O-H). Condensed/contracted formula: groups written together, connectivity preserved — ethane CH3CH3, ethanol CH3CH2OH (C2H5OH), acetic acid CH3COOH, dimethyl ether CH3OCH3.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Bond-line notation is the default of research literature because a 30-carbon natural product needs one zig-zag instead of a page of dashes.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Three Ways to Write One Molecule A molecular formula says what is in a molecule but not how it is joined. Chemistry needs three sharper notations: the **structural formula** (every bond drawn), the **contracted (condensed) formula** (groups written together), and the **bond-line (skeletal) formula** (lines only, carbons implicit).…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Molecular formula — the starting point - Shows the **actual number of each atom**: C₂H₆O. It cannot distinguish ethanol from dimethyl ether — both are C₂H₆O. ### 2.2 Structural formula - **Every bond is shown explicitly**, usually as dashes: H–C–C–O–H with all H's placed. Fully displays connectivity — which atom is joined to which.…  ·  ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Molecular formula** | Actual number of atoms of each element | C₂H₆O | | **Structural formula** | All bonds shown explicitly | H–C–C–O–H fully drawn | | **Condensed formula** | Groups written together, intra-group bonds omitted | CH₃CH₂OH | | **Bond-line formula** | Lines only; C and H on C…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Electrons orbit in fixed paths like planets. ✅ Electrons exist in probability clouds (orbitals).  ·  ❌ Heisenberg uncertainty means we cannot measure position and momentum precisely simultaneously — not that we lack good instruments.  ·  ❌ de Broglie wavelength applies only to light. ✅ All matter has wave nature; detectable mainly for small masses like electrons.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Quantum number l can be any integer. ✅ l ranges from 0 to n−1.  ·  ❌ Magnetic quantum number ml determines energy. ✅ ml determines orbital orientation, not energy (in absence of magnetic field).  ·  ❌ Spin quantum number ms can be ±½ or any value. ✅ ms is always +½ or −½.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Aufbau principle means filling from bottom to top of the diagram. ✅ Fill lowest-energy orbitals first: 1s→2s→2p→3s→3p→4s→3d→4p→...  ·  ❌ Pauli exclusion allows two electrons per orbital with any spin. ✅ Two electrons in same orbital must have opposite spins.  ·  ❌ Hund's rule means pair electrons before spreading. ✅ Electrons fill degenerate orbitals singly first with parallel spins.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ The mole is just a number like dozen. ✅ 1 mole = 6.022×10²³ particles (Avogadro constant) — a bridge between atomic and macroscopic scales.  ·  ❌ Molar mass and molecular mass are the same thing. ✅ Molecular mass is in amu; molar mass is in g/mol — numerically equal but different units.  ·  ❌ Limiting reagent is the reactant with smallest mass. ✅ Limiting reagent is the one that produces the least product (determined by moles, not mass).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ % yield can exceed 100%. ✅ % yield >100% indicates impure product or incomplete drying.  ·  ❌ Molarity and molality are the same. ✅ Molarity = mol/L solution (changes with T); Molality = mol/kg solvent (temperature-independent).  ·  ❌ A strong acid completely ionizes in water. ✅ Strong acids (HCl, HNO₃, H₂SO₄) are ~100% ionized; weak acids partially ionize.
